what: Which token set is which, and which run used which. Written because not knowing cost two training runs.
why: train/run.py defaults --tokens-dir to artifacts/tokens. That default is the OLDEST corpus in the directory. Two v0.77.0 runs were launched without the flag and compared against a baseline trained on a different corpus; the resulting ~1.3 nat 'gap' was nearly attributed to beta2 0.95 and nearly cost a working config.

token_sets.note: The DEFAULT --tokens-dir, and the oldest. This is the trap.
The frozen EVALUATION set used by scripts/evaluate.py comparisons, which is a separate role from training data.
THE DIALOGUE CORPUS. Built seven minutes before checkpoints-1024-dialogue's first checkpoint. This is what the current designated model trained on, and what any comparison against it must use.

how_tokens-v4_was_identified: By mtime against the baseline's checkpoint timestamps, corroborated by throughput: the dialogue run reached step 2000 in about six minutes, which requires ddp 4 at ~5.3 it/s, and a matched ddp-4 rerun reproduces that rate. No run log survives for that baseline -- only val_losses.jsonl -- which is itself the underlying problem.
the_actual_lesson: A run that does not record its own --tokens-dir cannot be compared to anything later. checkpoints-1024-dialogue has no train.log; checkpoints-ts10-b-s5489 does, which is the only reason its config was knowable at all.
suggested_fix: train/run.py should write a run manifest into --checkpoint-dir next to val_losses.jsonl: tokens dir and token counts, resolved optimizer block, seed, ddp, steps, batch, seq_len, tt-metal version. Not implemented yet.

PROOF_2026-08-19.was: Inferred from mtime (tokens-v4 built seven minutes before the first checkpoint) plus a throughput argument. Circumstantial.
PROOF_2026-08-19.now: PROVEN from the checkpoint's own header: tt_tnt_step00002000.pkl carries corpus_tokens = 391,823,393, and tokens-v4 is 352,641,058 train + 39,182,335 val = 391,823,393 exactly. No other token set in the directory sums to that.
PROOF_2026-08-19.still_unknown: The SEED. The checkpoint header does not record it and the directory has no run_manifest.json. So whether that baseline shared data order with the v0.77.0 runs -- which is what makes matched-step deltas sensitive rather than noisy -- cannot be established. Every comparison against it inherits that gap.
PROOF_2026-08-19.why_it_matters_concretely: The beta2 control run shows that two same-seed runs differing in one optimizer knob stay within +/-0.072 at any matched step. This morning's v077-vs-dialogue deltas reached +/-0.18. If the seeds matched, that scatter was real signal from the combined change; if they did not, it was data-order noise. The two readings have opposite consequences and cannot be told apart.

suggested_fix_upgraded.was: train/run.py should write a run manifest into --checkpoint-dir.  [DONE 2026-08-19]
suggested_fix_upgraded.better: train/checkpoint.py already writes a rich header into every .pkl -- vocab, seq_len, batch, corpus_tokens, model config, tokenizer dir, weights dtype. It is nearly a manifest already and it TRAVELS WITH THE ARTIFACT, surviving directory moves and renames in a way a sibling json does not. Adding seed, tokens_dir, the resolved optimizer block and ddp to that header would make every checkpoint self-describing. Not implemented.
